## Introduction

- Rise in type 2 prevalence, more individuals with young onset

- A key driver of these rates = Intergenerational trasmission – briefly discuss impact

- Pregnancy: a critical period for intervention - high motivation for behavioural changes and more frequent contact with healthcare providers

- Pregnancy: a metabolic stress test/period of metabolic vulnerability - can reveal individuals at high risk. One of the most prominent risk factors for future type 2 diabetes is GDM –tenfold risk. Beyond GDM other pregnancy complications have been linked to an increased risk of T2DM including LGA babies, preterm delivery and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (cit <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8114492/> and <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38723259/> )

- DP-Next is a project aiming to develop large scale diabetes risk prediction models for the entire population of Denmark using data from the nationwide registers. A key focus population for these prediction models is women post pregnancy. The rationale behind this decision combines clinical need and data availability. First, due to frequent contact with healthcare, there is an abundance of data. Additionally, women post pregnancy, including those with established risk factors underserved population & room for prevention .

- Literature has highlighted the need to understand what is driving the risk profile we need to understand trends in risk factors and outcomes.

- In this context, we aimed to investigate and describe trends in prevalence of key demographic and health related characteristics/ type 2 diabetes risk factors of pregnant women in Denmark over the last two decades, alongsize a summary of their calculated risk.

## Methods

-Data Sources and Cohort Definition

This was a longitudinal register-based study using data from the Danish National/Nationwide Registers.

- Coupling of mother PNR and child PNR

- Date of birth of child is the index date

- Subtracting gestational age from date to define the pregnancy date

In the Danish registers, each individual is assigned a PNR (from CPR but de-identified)

The study cohort included all pregnancies recorded within the danish nationwide registries between ... and ....

For each pregnancy contributing to the study population, the index date was defined as...

Individuals who were diagnosed with type 1 or type 2 diabetes at index date (?) were excluded.

The risk prediction model involved a subset of this cohort including only pregnancies occuring 2010 and 2015

Diagnoses of type 2 diabetes were identified using the OSDC algorithm.

Covariate Definitions

All covariates of interest were recorded at three time periods: pre-pregnancy, during and at delivery. Pre-pregnancy variables were measured

BMI:

Diagnoses of GDM, Pre-Eclampsia/Eclampsia and PMOS

Statistical model

This model is aimed at predicting the the 10 year risk of type 2 diabetes. All models will be incorporated into a super learner which will select the best performing model using cross-validation based on the Brier score. (citation)
